ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, CE is the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle ACD$ of $\triangle ABC$. If $\angle B = 30^\circ$ and $\angle ACE = 60^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle A$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $CE$ bisects $\angle ACD$ and $\angle ACE=60^\circ$,

it follows that $\angle ACD=2\angle ACE=120^\circ$.

Since $\angle ACD$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$ and $\angle B=30^\circ$,

it follows that $\angle ACD=\angle B+\angle A$,

thus $\angle A=\angle ACD-\angle B$

$=120^\circ-30^\circ$

$=\boxed{90^\circ}$.
